documents.title: Responsible Use of Generative AI
documents.summary: Provost page that defines generative AI, states university values, and gives faculty considerations on communicating a syllabus policy, protecting data, accountability and research-related disclosure. It names the default that unauthorized student AI use is cheating and points to Copilot and an IT tool-evaluation service.
documents.stance_why: The page states a default ("using AI tools as a substitute for their authentic intellectual and creative work is cheating unless instructors say otherwise") but is framed as "Faculty Considerations" telling instructors to "Communicate your policy on AI tool use", so the decision on use is handed to instructors.

units.why: Defines GAI as a system that generates content "in response to a prompt" from large data sets; it sets what the page covers, so informs/general and P61.
units.anchor: generative artificial intelligence (GAI) is a system that relies on very large data sets to

units.why: States that "the quality of GAI output varies in terms of accuracy and bias"; a factual statement about bias and accuracy, so P53 rather than P31 which tells students to verify.
units.anchor: the quality of GAI output varies in terms of accuracy and bias
units.fit_note: Also says output accuracy varies (P31) but no duty to verify is stated.

units.why: The university "supports the thoughtful application" of GAI to education, research and administration "when appropriate": a value statement that welcomes AI conditionally, an institution-wide framework (P56).
units.anchor: supports the thoughtful application of new technologies, such as generative artificial intelligence (GAI), to education,

units.why: Says GAI is "not a substitute" for human-to-human education and research; a principle in the framework (P56), also a reason AI should not replace human work.
units.anchor: GAI, provide support for but are not a substitute for these processes
units.fit_note: Also expresses that AI should not replace human interaction (close to P32/P41) but is stated as a university value.

units.why: Says GAI "should not reduce equitable access" or impinge on rights such as privacy and due process; an equity and rights principle assigned to P56 as the framework statement.
units.anchor: The use of GAI should not reduce equitable access to a human-centered, effective, and quality
units.fit_note: Also an equity/rights statement (P51) but framed as an institutional principle.

units.why: The Joint Task Force "reached consensus" on the values: says how and by whom the guidance was produced, so P84.
units.anchor: Joint Task Force on Generative A.I.

units.why: Tells faculty to "Communicate your policy on AI tool use to your students": instructors must make expectations explicit, so P09.
units.anchor: Communicate your policy on AI tool use to your students

units.why: "Absent a statement in the syllabus, students are advised to check with their instructor": tells students to ask the instructor when unsure, so P10; the default of cheating is a separate sentence coded as P06.
units.anchor: Absent a statement in the syllabus, students are advised to check with their instructor

units.why: "If you permit the use of these tools, please tell students how you want their use documented or disclosed": asks instructors who allow AI to specify disclosure; P24 is the closest disclosure type though it is addressed to instructors.
units.anchor: please tell students how you want their use documented or disclosed
units.fit_note: Addressed to instructors to specify the disclosure method rather than to students to disclose.

units.why: "the default is that using AI tools as a substitute for their authentic intellectual and creative work is cheating unless instructors say otherwise" sets the default and its exception, so P06 (fallback) is more exact than P01 since instructors can lift it.
units.anchor: using AI tools as a substitute for their authentic intellectual and creative work is cheating
units.fit_note: Also classifies the substitute use as cheating (P36).

units.why: "don’t enter personal information, copyrighted text, images, or video, and don’t enter protected information about others": a ban on inputting personal or protected data into AI, so P50.
units.anchor: Don’t enter personal information, copyrighted text, images, or video, and don’t enter protected information about

units.why: Entered data "will become part of the model used to train that tool in the future": a fact about tools keeping prompts, which is the reason for data protection, P50.
units.anchor: will become part of the model used to train that tool in the future

units.why: "Some university tools may provide additional data privacy protections": points users to institution-provided tools with better privacy; P50 prefers vetted tools.
units.anchor: Some university tools may provide additional data privacy protections

units.why: Task force recommendations urge mindfulness when applying GAI to "evaluating scholarship applications, summarizing or checking student work, and offering ranking suggestions": caution about AI in decisions about people; P73 fits better than P46 because scholarships and rankings are included.
units.anchor: traditionally human activities such as evaluating scholarship applications, summarizing or checking student work
units.fit_note: A call for mindfulness, not a ban on AI in these decisions.

units.why: "these tools make mistakes. They can give wrong information, fake information": warns that output is unreliable, so P31.
units.anchor: They can give wrong information, fake information, include copyrighted content, give biased results
units.fit_note: Also mentions copyrighted content and bias; no explicit duty to verify.

units.why: "It is a good idea to help graduate students be aware of these policies at the outset of a project": recommends that advisors make graduate students aware of funder and venue AI policies, a research rule (P62).
units.anchor: help graduate students be aware of these policies at the outset of a project

units.why: "you are just as responsible for the content of that work as if you had only used your brain": the user owns AI-assisted output, so P29.
units.anchor: you are just as responsible for the content of that work as if you had

units.why: Points to Center for Teaching and Learning information "that instructors experimenting with GAI may find useful": support for faculty learning about AI, P63.
units.anchor: instructors experimenting with GAI may find useful

units.why: "IT provides an evaluation service of AI tools from a security standpoint": the university reviews AI tools for security, P65.
units.anchor: IT provides an evaluation service of AI tools from a security standpoint

units.why: Copilot "protects user data and does not use user data to train models" when logged in with a NetID under the university license: names a licensed, privacy-protecting tool, P92 (institution-wide) rather than P17 because it is not course-specific.
units.anchor: Copilot which protects user data and does not use user data to train models when

units.why: "unauthorized use of GAI by students to complete coursework is in violation of the academic honesty policy": classes unauthorized AI use as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: unauthorized use of GAI by students to complete coursework is in violation of the academic

units.why: Researchers seeking funding "may want to review" NIH and NSF guidelines on GAI in proposals and review panels: defers to funder rules, P62.
units.anchor: Researchers seeking external funding may want to review the guidelines on the use of GAI

units.why: "scholars should familiarize themselves with the GAI use and disclosure policies of publication venues": defers to venue policies on AI use and disclosure, P62.
units.anchor: scholars should familiarize themselves with the GAI use and disclosure policies of publication venues

units.why: "Researchers are encouraged to search for and verify publisher guidance ... before incorporating GAI tools into their research": check publisher rules before using AI in research, P62.
units.anchor: Researchers are encouraged to search for and verify publisher guidance on the use of GAI

documents.title: Guidance on Generative Artificial Intelligence
documents.summary: Undergraduate Student Success Center page applying the Academic Integrity Policy to generative AI. It sets a default of no AI without explicit instructor permission, asks instructors to state expectations in syllabi, warns about AI wearables and detectors, and outlines the first steps for suspected misuse.
documents.stance_why: The page says "Students cannot use Generative AI (chatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, etc.) to complete any academic work without instructor permission", so AI is banned unless the instructor permits it.

units.why: The page explains "how the use of genAI fits into our Academic Integrity policy" for students, faculty and staff and names the terms GenAI, AI, chatbots: a scope statement, P61.
units.anchor: how the use of genAI fits into our Academic Integrity policy on this page of
units.fit_note: Scope statement for the page rather than a definition of AI.

units.why: "Students cannot use Generative AI ... to complete any academic work without instructor permission" bans AI unless permitted, the default prohibition itself, P01.
units.anchor: Students cannot use Generative AI (chatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, etc.) to complete any academic work without

units.why: "If an instructor has not given explicit permission ... students should assume they are not allowed": states what applies when the syllabus is silent, P06.
units.anchor: If an instructor has not given explicit permission to use Generative AI, students should assume

units.why: "Students should always receive instructor permission to use Generative AI in any part of completing academic work": students must get permission before using AI, P10.
units.anchor: Students should always receive instructor permission to use Generative AI in any part of completing

units.why: "Instructors should have clear expectations on Generative AI use in their courses, available to students in their course syllabus": syllabus statement expected, P09.
units.anchor: Instructors should have clear expectations on Generative AI use in their courses, available to students

units.why: "We also suggest instructors cover this policy in their courses at the beginning of the semester": tells instructors to discuss the policy with students at the start, P66, not P09 because it goes beyond the syllabus line.
units.anchor: cover this policy in their courses at the beginning of the semester

units.why: "consider including specific guidelines for different types of assignments": suggests assignment-level rules so the rule can vary by assignment, P04.
units.anchor: consider including specific guidelines for different types of assignments

units.why: Lists university resources on AI (IDEAS, College of Education) for people who want "to learn more": pointers to AI learning materials, P70 as the closest type.
units.anchor: Check out the resources provided by Instructional Design, Engagement, and Support (IDEAS) on GenAI
units.fit_note: Pointers to resources, not training or a mandated module.

units.why: The policy "states that students cannot use or attempt to use unauthorized materials including generative AI tools in any academic exercise without instructor permission": restates that unauthorized AI is an integrity violation, P36.
units.anchor: students cannot use or attempt to use unauthorized materials including generative AI tools in any

units.why: Repeats that students "should assume that they cannot use generative AI tools in a course unless their instructor has given them explicit permission": a silent-syllabus fallback restated in different words, coded as its own statement under P06.
units.anchor: Students should assume that they cannot use generative AI tools in a course unless their

units.why: "Instructors are encouraged to address the use of generative AI tools in their syllabus and in course discussions about academic integrity": encourages syllabus statement and class discussion; P66 since discussion is the added element.
units.anchor: Instructors are encouraged to address the use of generative AI tools in their syllabus and
units.fit_note: Also encourages the syllabus statement (P09).

units.why: "Instructors should communicate their policy on generative AI ... in their course syllabus and assignment instructions": the syllabus and assignment statement requirement, P09.
units.anchor: Instructors should communicate their policy on generative AI communicated in their course syllabus and assignment

units.why: Wearable smart devices "with built-in video/audio recording capabilities and/or generative AI assistance ... may pose risks when it comes to securing assessments": warns that AI-enabled glasses and watches threaten assessments, P07.
units.anchor: wearable smart devices with built-in video/audio recording capabilities and/or generative AI assistance, such as watches

units.why: "Instructors should specify their expectations regarding use of wearable smart devices in their course syllabus": tells instructors to put the rule on AI-capable wearables in the syllabus, P07 because the topic is the device rule.
units.anchor: Instructors should specify their expectations regarding use of wearable smart devices in their course syllabus
units.fit_note: Also a syllabus-statement duty (P09).

units.why: "Students should verify use of such devices is allowed prior to using them": students check before using AI-capable wearables; the subject is P07, where a reader looks for device rules.
units.anchor: Students should verify use of such devices is allowed prior to using them
units.fit_note: Also an ask-before-using duty (P10).

units.why: "the first step is to notify the student and request a meeting to discuss the situation": talk with the student before escalating, P57.
units.anchor: the first step is to notify the student and request a meeting to discuss the

units.why: Links Center for Teaching and Learning guidance on suspected misuse for "strategies for prevention, identification, and measured response": points to a resource on a measured response, P68 as nearest.
units.anchor: strategies for prevention, identification, and measured response
units.fit_note: Only points to a resource; "measured response" is the only cue.

units.why: "AI detectors can produce false negatives and false positives": detectors are unreliable, P39.
units.anchor: AI detectors can produce false negatives and false positives in their reporting

units.why: "use of these tools may raise data and privacy concerns": detector use raises privacy issues, a second reason against detectors; P39 is where a reader looks for detector cautions.
units.anchor: use of these tools may raise data and privacy concerns
units.fit_note: Adds a privacy concern, not only unreliability.

units.why: "The Academic Integrity Office does not recommend relying on detection tool reports": advises against relying on detectors, P39.
units.anchor: does not recommend relying on detection tool reports when addressing suspected academic misconduct

units.why: Instead of detector reports, "identify components of the student’s work that raise concerns and ask the student to address those concerns directly in a conversation": gather concerns and talk with the student first, P57.
units.anchor: identify components of the student’s work that raise concerns and ask the student to address

units.why: "If ... the instructor still suspects academic misconduct, they should report the incident following the reporting procedures in the policy": formal reporting step, P81.
units.anchor: they should report the incident following the reporting procedures in the policy

documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy
documents.summary: Faculty Senate academic integrity policy. Generative AI appears in the definitions of cheating and plagiarism, and the rest covers instructor duties, the informal and formal process, and student rights. It requires instructors to state expectations, including permission or restriction of AI tools.
documents.stance_why: The policy lists as cheating the "use of unauthorized materials, including generative AI tools ... (unless explicitly permitted by instructor)", so AI is barred unless an instructor permits it, although the document is a general integrity policy that leaves course rules to instructors.

units.why: The infraction "Cheating" includes "unauthorized materials, including generative AI tools ... (unless explicitly permitted by instructor)": unauthorized AI use is classed as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: unauthorized materials, including generative AI tools, assistance, collaboration, information, or study aids in any academic
units.fit_note: Also sets a default ban lifted by explicit instructor permission (P06).

units.why: Plagiarism is "representing the words, ideas, art, and/or creative works of another, including generative AI tools, as one's own work": presenting AI output as one's own is the offence; P36 (misconduct) rather than P45 because AI is not framed as a human collaborator.
units.anchor: representing the words, ideas, art, and/or creative works of another, including generative AI tools, as
units.fit_note: Also says submitting AI output as own work is the offence (P19).

units.why: "Instructors may analyze student work, electronically or by other means, for originality of content": permits originality checking of student work, P40; it does not name AI.
units.anchor: Instructors may analyze student work, electronically or by other means, for originality of content
units.fit_note: Does not mention AI; general originality checking.

units.why: "Instructors may include student work in databases for the purpose of checking for possible plagiarized content": allows submitting student work to plagiarism-check databases, P40.
units.anchor: Instructors may include student work in databases for the purpose of checking for possible plagiarized
units.fit_note: Does not mention AI.

units.why: "Instructors are to be clear about the expectations in their course(s)/assignment(s) of how work should be completed": instructors must state expectations, P09.
units.anchor: Instructors are to be clear about the expectations in their course(s)/assignment(s) of how work should
units.fit_note: Does not mention AI here; general expectations.

units.why: "Instructors are to provide guidance to students, ideally within the syllabus and/or within specific assignment guidelines": syllabus guidance duty for instructors, P09.
units.anchor: Instructors are to provide guidance to students, ideally within the syllabus and/or within specific assignment

units.why: "students are to adhere to that guidance": students must follow the course-level rules; a separate student duty, P78.
units.anchor: students are to adhere to that guidance

units.why: "Expectations within assignments may vary across courses; ... students should be familiar with individual course policies": rules vary per course and students must know them, P78; P11 not chosen since it does not say one course does not carry over.
units.anchor: students should be familiar with individual course policies
units.fit_note: Also says expectations vary by course (P04).

units.why: "Students are responsible for completing all work within the parameters set forth by instructors": students must work within instructor limits, which include AI limits; P78 rather than P29 because the duty is about following parameters.
units.anchor: Students are responsible for completing all work within the parameters set forth by instructors

units.why: "University policies on academic integrity apply across all courses": a university-wide baseline for every course, P56.
units.anchor: University policies on academic integrity apply across all courses
units.fit_note: Does not mention AI.

units.why: "In cases with genuine misunderstanding ... instructors and students should be in communication with each other to take steps to remedy the coursework": a misunderstanding leads to talking and remedy, an educative response, P68.
units.anchor: instructors and students should be in communication with each other to take steps to remedy
units.fit_note: Does not mention AI.

units.why: "Any violation ... will result in negative consequences that may hinder an individual assignment grade, course grade, academic progress, or university enrollment": states consequences in general terms without a fixed penalty, P37 as nearest.
units.anchor: will result in negative consequences that may hinder an individual assignment grade, course grade, academic
units.fit_note: Gives categories of consequences, not specific penalties.

units.why: "if there is a misunderstanding so egregious that common sense would indicate a different course of action, instructors may choose to pursue academic sanctions": sets a threshold for sanctioning despite misunderstanding, nearest P69.
units.anchor: if there is a misunderstanding so egregious that common sense would indicate a different course
units.fit_note: Sets a threshold for sanctioning despite misunderstanding rather than a proof standard.

units.why: When "student-staff ... suspect an academic integrity infraction, they should report their concerns to their supervisor": staff reporting duty, P81.
units.anchor: they should report their concerns to their supervisor

units.why: "Graduate TAs are responsible for reporting to the instructor of record any suspicions of academic dishonesty": TA reporting step, P81.
units.anchor: Graduate TAs are responsible for reporting to the instructor of record any suspicions of academic

units.why: "All reported cases of academic integrity infractions will go through and be held by the Academic Integrity Office": names the office that owns and holds cases, P80.
units.anchor: All reported cases of academic integrity infractions will go through and be held by the

units.why: Instructors "are responsible for contacting the student(s)" with a request to meet once they suspect an infraction: a talk-first duty, P57. The deadline is split across a line break in the source, so the anchor stops before it.
units.anchor: Once an instructor suspects an academic integrity infraction, they are responsible for contacting the student(s)

units.why: "Students are responsible for engaging in communication with their instructor ... ignoring or otherwise avoiding instructor outreach will not result in a suspension of the process": students must engage, a procedural step, P81.
units.anchor: ignoring or otherwise avoiding instructor outreach will not result in a suspension of the process

units.why: "the instructor may assign a grade penalty commensurate with the infraction" after mutual agreement: penalty set by the instructor, nearest P37.
units.anchor: the instructor may assign a grade penalty commensurate with the infraction
units.fit_note: Penalty is "commensurate", with suggestions in an appendix not in this text; no fixed penalty.

units.why: "The student(s) and the instructor(s) will both sign the informal resolution form": informal resolution procedure with a form, P81.
units.anchor: The student(s) and the instructor(s) will both sign the informal resolution form

units.why: An instructor who sanctions without consultation "must maintain communication outreach documents" and submit them with the Non-Communication Form: a reporting procedure, P81.
units.anchor: the instructor must maintain communication outreach documents that demonstrate non-responsiveness from the student

units.why: "if three or more forms per student are filed ... further disciplinary action": escalation by number of offences stated in advance, P37.
units.anchor: if three or more forms per student are filed, the Academic Integrity Office will connect
units.fit_note: Escalation by number of forms, not a stated grade penalty.

units.why: "If no agreement can be made via an informal resolution, this will trigger a formal resolution": the formal route, P81.
units.anchor: If no agreement can be made via an informal resolution, this will trigger a formal

units.why: "there will be both course sanctions as well as a notification on the student(s) official academic record" if a hearing finds dishonesty: consequences stated in advance, P37.
units.anchor: there will be both course sanctions as well as a notification on the student(s) official

units.why: Instructors "Will provide clear guidelines in syllabus and/or individual course assignments", with an example "permission/restriction of generative AI tools": the instructor duty names AI explicitly, P09.
units.anchor: permission/restriction of generative AI tools

units.why: "Will make a good-faith effort to communicate proactively with student(s) when an academic integrity infraction is suspected": instructor talks with the student first, P57.
units.anchor: Will make a good-faith effort to communicate proactively with student(s) when an academic integrity infraction

units.why: "Will not assign a grade on the basis of suspicion": a limit on sanctions requiring more than suspicion, an evidence standard, P69.
units.anchor: Will not assign a grade on the basis of suspicion

units.why: Students have the right to "A conversation with their instructor about what occurred within a prescribed time frame": a right in the process, P64.
units.anchor: A conversation with their instructor about what occurred within a prescribed time frame

units.why: "The opportunity to reject the informal process; ... they may initiate a formal hearing": right to contest an allegation, P64.
units.anchor: if the student feels they have completed the work with academic integrity, they may initiate

units.why: Students may "Grieve a grade sanction imposed that did not follow the process": a further right of the accused, P64.
units.anchor: Grieve a grade sanction imposed that did not follow the process outlined in the Academic

units.why: Students have the right to "Clarity on resources for support in understanding the process, including academic advisors, the Ombuds office": directs accused students to human help, P72.
units.anchor: Clarity on resources for support in understanding the process, including academic advisors, the Ombuds office
